title: Termwise product cones remain limiting in the derived category
statement: Let A be an abelian category with countable products satisfying CountableAB4Star and a chosen derived category. For every countable type J and family C of integer-indexed cochain complexes in A, the image under DerivedCategory.Q of the termwise product limit cone of C is a limit cone. No products in the derived category are assumed.

proof.text: The quotient from complexes to the homotopy category preserves products by HomotopyCategory.isLimitFanQuotient: chain maps and homotopies assemble componentwise. Exact countable limits commute with short-complex homology (apply preservation of homology to the limit functor), hence with complex homology via the three-term short-complex functor. Descend this preservation along the essentially surjective quotient. The homology comparison for a product identifies the homology map of the product of quasi-isomorphisms with a product of isomorphisms, so quasi-isomorphisms in the homotopy category are stable under these products.

For an arbitrary cone vertex choose its preimage under the localization and the canonical isomorphism. Represent each component by a left fraction, assemble its numerators by Pi.lift and its denominators by Pi.map. Stability under products makes the assembled denominator invertible. Compose the assembled numerator with its inverse and the vertex isomorphism to obtain the lift. Verify each projection by cancelling its component denominator and using Pi.map_π and Pi.lift_π.

First consider an original homotopy-category map a into the product whose localized components vanish. The left-fraction equality criterion map_eq_iff_postcomp supplies a quasi-isomorphism out of each factor killing the corresponding component. Their product is a quasi-isomorphism, and postcomposing a with it is zero by product extensionality; invert this product to conclude that the localized a is zero. For an arbitrary localized map use a right fraction, cancel its invertible denominator to reduce to the preceding assertion. Apply this zero criterion to the difference of two lifts, after transporting the vertex by essential surjectivity. Fan.IsLimit.mk now supplies the universal property. Compose preservation for the quotient and Qh via quotientCompQhIso and apply isLimitOfPreserves to the specified termwise limit cone.

proof_origin.place: Lemma lemma-products (Tag 07KC); complete uniqueness argument via left/right fraction equality criteria, reusing the proved private helpers of DerivedCountableProductsProperties

lean.statement:
theorem derivedCategory_termwiseProduct_isLimit
    (A : Type u) [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    [HasCountableProducts A] [CountableAB4Star A]
    (J : Type) [Countable J] (C : J → CochainComplex A ℤ) :
    Nonempty (IsLimit (DerivedCategory.Q.mapCone (limit.cone (Discrete.functor C))))
